description: Composite figure of five unlabelled panels arranged in two rows, mixing mechanical-property plots with TEM micrographs. Top row, two dual-axis plots sharing the axes True Stress (MPa) on the left (0-1600) and Strain Hardening Rate dσ/dε (MPa) on the right (0-4000), with True Strain on x. The left plot (a) runs to roughly 0.35 True Strain and shows solid (true stress) and dashed (strain-hardening rate) curves, colour-coded black, red and blue and tagged by arrows as 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr; it represents the near-rapidly solidified strip condition. A large yellow arrow labelled "Cold-rolling with reduction of 20%" points from (a) to the right plot (b), which plots the same three alloys to about 0.25 True Strain after cold rolling and shows different curve ordering and peaks. Bottom row: three bright-field TEM micrographs labelled 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr, each with a 500 nm scale bar, a yellow arrow marking (111) planar/slip features, and an inset selected-area diffraction spot pattern indexed [1̄10]. The figure argues that the Cr-dependent deformation substructure imaged in the TEM panels underlies the stress and strain-hardening responses plotted above. No numeric values are printed on any panel.

subfigures.description: Top-left dual-axis plot: True Stress (MPa) 0-1600 (left axis) and Strain Hardening Rate dσ/dε (MPa) 0-4000 (right axis) versus True Strain (0.00 to about 0.35). Solid curves are true stress and dashed curves are strain-hardening rate for three conditions tagged 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr. No numeric values are printed; the stress curves peak between the 1200 and 1600 MPa gridlines.

Top-right dual-axis plot with the same two y-axes and True Strain from 0.00 to 0.25, reached across a large yellow arrow reading "Cold-rolling with reduction of 20%". Same 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr colour-coded solid/dashed curve pairs, but with different peak positions and hardening-rate decay than (a).
Bright-field TEM micrograph labelled 0Cr with a 500 nm scale bar, dense planar deformation bands marked by a yellow arrow labelled (111), and an inset SAED spot pattern indexed [1̄10].
Bright-field TEM micrograph labelled 3Cr with a 500 nm scale bar, planar slip bands/lamellae marked with a yellow arrow labelled (111), and an inset SAED spot pattern indexed [1̄10].
Bright-field TEM micrograph labelled 6Cr with a 500 nm scale bar, fine planar deformation features marked with a yellow arrow labelled (111), and an inset SAED spot pattern indexed [1̄10].

observations.observation: The figure is composite: two dual-axis mechanical-property plots occupy the top row and three bright-field TEM micrographs form the bottom row.
Both top plots use the same axes: True Stress (MPa) on the left (tick range 0-1600) and Strain Hardening Rate dσ/dε (MPa) on the right (tick range 0-4000), with True Strain on x.
The x-axis (True Strain) range differs between the two plots: the left plot extends to about 0.35 while the right plot extends only to about 0.25.
Both plots contain three colour-coded curve pairs tagged by arrows as 0Cr (black), 3Cr (red) and 6Cr (blue); solid lines are true stress, dashed lines are strain-hardening rate.

A large yellow arrow labelled "Cold-rolling with reduction of 20%" separates the left (as-solidified) plot from the right (cold-rolled) plot, indicating the two plots are before/after states of the same three alloys.
The three bottom TEM micrographs are labelled 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr and each carries a 500 nm scale bar.

Each TEM panel contains an inset selected-area electron diffraction spot pattern indexed [1̄10], consistent with a BCC/B2-type ferritic matrix viewed along a <110>-type zone axis (interpretation of the index, not printed text).
In all three TEM panels a yellow arrow points to planar features annotated with a plane index that appears to read (111).
The stress curves in both top plots rise steeply at low strain and flatten near maximum between the 1200 and 1600 MPa gridlines; no peak value is printed anywhere.
The dashed strain-hardening-rate curves in both plots start near the 3000-4000 MPa gridlines at low strain and decay steeply, dropping below the stress curves at higher strain.
No caption was extracted for this figure, so no caption-stated values, conditions or panel letters are available; all panel identities above come from the pixels.

The paper abstract states that Cr addition increased the volume fraction and size of δ-ferrite and decreased κ-carbide precipitation in near-rapidly solidified Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C (wt.%) steel strips, and that yield strength decreased significantly while ultimate tensile strength and total elongation changed.

unreadable_items: No numeric data labels are printed on either top plot; peak stress and maximum strain-hardening-rate values can only be read relative to gridlines, so exact values cannot be extracted.
The plane index written beside the yellow arrows in the TEM panels is small and partially readable; it appears as (111) but is not fully certain.
Panel letters (a)-(e) are not printed on the figure; the lettering used here is the reading-order assignment.
TEM inset SAED patterns are small and diffraction spots cannot be indexed beyond the printed [1̄10] zone-axis label.
No caption was provided, so panel-specific conditions (e.g. which condition is as-solidified vs cold-rolled beyond the arrow text) are inferred from the layout.
